name: SlackMCP
title: Slack
description: Send messages, search, and read a Slack workspace
whenToUse: Pick to reach a Slack workspace: post a message or thread reply, search messages, read a channel's history, list channels, look up a user, or react to a post. Attach it to an agent so it can talk to a team, or trigger it directly to post to a default channel.

inputs.name: input
inputs.description: Trigger. When the graph runs this node it posts a message, taking { channel, text } from here, falling back to the configured default channel.

outputs.name: output
outputs.description: The Slack API response for whatever ran

defaultChannel.title: Default Channel
defaultChannel.description: Channel ID used when the workflow triggers this node directly. Not used for MCP tool calls. A channel ID, e.g. C01ABC123, not a name.

authRequired.title: Require sign-in
authRequired.description: Only a signed-in caller may run this step. Leave off and it runs for whoever the workflow's trigger admitted, which is the usual answer.

authRole.title: Require role
authRole.description: A claim the caller's account must carry, as noun:verb (finance:approve, payments:refund). Leave blank to require only that they are signed in.

package.name: slack
package.packageFile:
$schema: https://docs.unoverse.ai/schemas/nodes/package.schema.json

# FULLY DECLARATIVE. One node, six MCP methods, one bearer token, nothing new required.
# The retired TypeScript is at `_legacy/nodes/slack/`.
#
# The credential carries an optional `host`, so the url is templated per workspace. AllowedHosts
# covers the default plus one subdomain level for an enterprise grid.

name: slack
displayName: Slack
description: Slack workspace integration for Unoverse
version: 2.0.0
category: communication
logoUrl: https://res.cloudinary.com/sonik/image/upload/v1779530623/gravity/icons/Slack.svg

features:
  - Send messages, including thread replies
  - Search messages and read channel history
  - List channels and look up users
  - Add reactions

allowedHosts:
  - slack.com
  - "*.slack.com"

requires:
  credential: [bearer]
  transport: [json]
  executorVersion: ">=1.0.0"

credentials.slackBotToken.yaml:
$schema: https://docs.unoverse.ai/schemas/nodes/credential.schema.json

name: slackBotToken
displayName: Slack
description: Slack Bot User OAuth Token for API access
documentationUrl: https://api.slack.com/authentication/token-types#bot

properties:
  - name: token
    displayName: Bot Token
    type: string
    required: true
    secret: true
    description: Bot User OAuth Token
    placeholder: xoxb-

  - name: host
    displayName: Host
    type: string
    required: false
    secret: false
    description: Slack API host. Defaults to slack.com.
    placeholder: slack.com

shared.api.yaml:
# What every Slack call shares.
#
# The host is optional on the credential and defaults to slack.com, and any scheme or
# trailing slash a person pasted is stripped. An expression rather than a template, because
# a blank `{{ }}` would produce `https:///api/...`.

credential: &credential
  scheme: bearer
  token: "{{ credentials.slackBotToken.token }}"

# Slack answers 200 with `ok: false` and an `error` code for almost every failure, including
# a bad token and a missing scope. Without this every method would look like it succeeded and
# hand back an empty result.
error: &error
  when: "return response.ok === false"
  message: "return response.error || 'slack rejected the request'"

files.api/events.yaml:
# One row, one connector.
#
# When the call was skipped there is no `calls.post`, and that is the misconfiguration case:
# it reports what is missing rather than emitting an empty success.

- emit: output
  from: response
  value: >-
    return calls.post
      ? calls.post
      : { ok: false, error: 'channel and text are required for workflow execution' }
files.api/run.yaml:
# Triggered by the graph, this node posts a message. The channel comes from the input or the
# configured default; the text comes from the input.
#
# Skipped when either is missing, so a misconfigured node says so rather than calling Slack
# with an empty message. The events row below turns the skip into a named error.

- name: post
  when: >-
    return !!((signal.input || {}).channel || config.defaultChannel)
      && !!((signal.input || {}).text || (signal.input || {}).input)
  method: POST
  url: "return 'https://' + String(credentials.slackBotToken.host || 'slack.com').replace('https://', '').replace('http://', '').split('/')[0] + '/api/chat.postMessage'"
  credential: { $ref: api#credential }
  body: >-
    return {
      channel: (signal.input || {}).channel || config.defaultChannel,
      text: String((signal.input || {}).text || (signal.input || {}).input)
    }
  transport: json
  error: { $ref: api#error }
files.api/service.yaml:
# The MCP methods an agent can call. Transcribed from src/SlackMCP/service/index.ts, with the
# descriptions from service/mcpSchema.ts, which are what a model reads when choosing a tool.
#
# Every method is one call to https://<host>/api/<slack method>. The host is optional on the
# credential and defaults to slack.com, with any scheme or path a person pasted stripped off.
#
# Slack answers 200 with `ok: false` for nearly every failure, including a bad token and a
# missing scope, so every call declares the shared `error` block. Without it each method would
# look like it succeeded and hand back nothing.

send_message:
  description: >-
    Send a message to a Slack channel or thread. Use the channel ID, not the name. To reply in
    a thread, pass thread_ts.
  calls:
    - name: post
      method: POST
      url: "return 'https://' + String(credentials.slackBotToken.host || 'slack.com').replace('https://', '').replace('http://', '').split('/')[0] + '/api/chat.postMessage'"
      credential: { $ref: api#credential }
      body: >-
        return Object.fromEntries(Object.entries({
          channel: params.channel,
          text: params.text,
          thread_ts: params.thread_ts
        }).filter(e => e[1] !== undefined && e[1] !== null && e[1] !== ''))
      transport: json
      error: { $ref: api#error }
  returns: "return { ok: true, ts: response.ts, channel: response.channel }"

list_channels:
  description: >-
    List public channels in the workspace, with name, id, topic and member count. Pass the
    cursor from a previous response to page.
  calls:
    - name: channels
      method: GET
      url: "return 'https://' + String(credentials.slackBotToken.host || 'slack.com').replace('https://', '').replace('http://', '').split('/')[0] + '/api/conversations.list'"
      credential: { $ref: api#credential }
      query:
        types: public_channel
        exclude_archived: "true"
        limit: "return String(Math.min(params.limit || 100, 200))"
        cursor: "{{ params.cursor }}"
      transport: json
      error: { $ref: api#error }
  returns: >-
    return {
      ok: true,
      channels: (response.channels || []).map(ch => ({
        id: ch.id,
        name: ch.name,
        topic: (ch.topic || {}).value || '',
        purpose: (ch.purpose || {}).value || '',
        num_members: ch.num_members
      })),
      has_more: !!((response.response_metadata || {}).next_cursor),
      next_cursor: (response.response_metadata || {}).next_cursor || null
    }

search_messages:
  description: >-
    Search messages matching a query. Supports Slack search syntax such as in:#channel and
    from:@user. Returns messages with channel context and timestamps.
  calls:
    - name: search
      method: GET
      url: "return 'https://' + String(credentials.slackBotToken.host || 'slack.com').replace('https://', '').replace('http://', '').split('/')[0] + '/api/search.messages'"
      credential: { $ref: api#credential }
      query:
        query: "{{ params.query }}"
        count: "return String(Math.min(params.count || 20, 100))"
      transport: json
      error: { $ref: api#error }
  returns: "return response"

get_user:
  description: >-
    Look up a user by email, or by user id when no email is given. Returns their Slack
    profile.
  calls:
    - name: byEmail
      method: GET
      url: "return 'https://' + String(credentials.slackBotToken.host || 'slack.com').replace('https://', '').replace('http://', '').split('/')[0] + '/api/users.lookupByEmail'"
      credential: { $ref: api#credential }
      when: "return !!params.email"
      query:
        email: "{{ params.email }}"
      transport: json
      error: { $ref: api#error }
    - name: byId
      method: GET
      url: "return 'https://' + String(credentials.slackBotToken.host || 'slack.com').replace('https://', '').replace('http://', '').split('/')[0] + '/api/users.info'"
      credential: { $ref: api#credential }
      when: "return !params.email && !!params.user_id"
      query:
        user: "{{ params.user_id }}"
      transport: json
      error: { $ref: api#error }
  # Whichever lookup ran. Neither means the caller passed nothing to look up, and that is a
  # structured refusal rather than a throw: an agent can correct itself from this.
  returns: >-
    return calls.byEmail || calls.byId
      || { ok: false, error: 'either user_id or email is required' }

read_history:
  description: >-
    Read recent messages from a channel, newest first. Bound the window with oldest and latest
    timestamps.
  calls:
    - name: history
      method: GET
      url: "return 'https://' + String(credentials.slackBotToken.host || 'slack.com').replace('https://', '').replace('http://', '').split('/')[0] + '/api/conversations.history'"
      credential: { $ref: api#credential }
      query:
        channel: "{{ params.channel }}"
        limit: "return String(Math.min(params.limit || 25, 100))"
        oldest: "{{ params.oldest }}"
        latest: "{{ params.latest }}"
      transport: json
      error: { $ref: api#error }
  returns: "return response"

add_reaction:
  description: Add an emoji reaction to a message, identified by its channel and timestamp.
  calls:
    - name: react
      method: POST
      url: "return 'https://' + String(credentials.slackBotToken.host || 'slack.com').replace('https://', '').replace('http://', '').split('/')[0] + '/api/reactions.add'"
      credential: { $ref: api#credential }
      body: >-
        return {
          channel: params.channel,
          timestamp: params.timestamp,
          name: String(params.name).split(':').join('')
        }
      transport: json
      error: { $ref: api#error }
  returns: "return { ok: true }"
files.config.yaml:
$schema: https://docs.unoverse.ai/schemas/nodes/config.schema.json

configSchema:
  type: object
  required: []
  properties:
    defaultChannel:
      type: string
      title: Default Channel
      description: >-
        Channel ID used when the workflow triggers this node directly. Not used for MCP tool
        calls. A channel ID, e.g. C01ABC123, not a name.
      default: ""
      "ui:field": template
"ui:order": [defaultChannel]
files.interface.yaml:
$schema: https://docs.unoverse.ai/schemas/nodes/interface.schema.json

inputs:
  - name: input
    type: object
    description: >-
      Trigger. When the graph runs this node it posts a message, taking { channel, text }
      from here, falling back to the configured default channel.

outputs:
  - name: output
    type: object
    description: The Slack API response for whatever ran

credentials:
  - name: slackBotToken
    required: true
    displayName: Slack

serviceConnectors:
  - name: mcpService
    serviceType: mcp
    isService: true
    methods: [send_message, list_channels, search_messages, get_user, read_history, add_reaction]
    description: >-
      MCP tools for an agent: send messages, search, list channels, look up users, read
      history, add reactions.
files.node.yaml:
$schema: https://docs.unoverse.ai/schemas/nodes/node.schema.json

type: SlackMCP
kind: PromiseNode
name: Slack
category: Communication
color: "#4A154B"
# Attached to an agent over a service edge rather than wired in sequence.
template: service
description: Send messages, search, and read a Slack workspace
whenToUse: >
  Pick to reach a Slack workspace: post a message or thread reply, search messages, read a
  channel's history, list channels, look up a user, or react to a post. Attach it to an
  agent so it can talk to a team, or trigger it directly to post to a default channel.

# WHO MAY RUN THIS (DECLARATIVE_NODES.md §9.13). Compulsory on every node, so that a node
# nobody thought about cannot look the same as one deliberately left open.
#
# `required: false` adds no requirement of its own: the node runs for whoever the trigger
# admitted. The trigger instance's publicEntry toggle still owns the door, and requirements
# only ever narrow.
auth:
  required: false

capabilities:
  # Sending a message is a side effect, so reuse must never stand in for it.
  cacheable: false
files.test.yaml:
$schema: https://docs.unoverse.ai/schemas/nodes/test.schema.json

# The workflow channel POSTS A MESSAGE, so this fixture deliberately omits the text: the run
# exercises composition, credentials and the skip path without writing to a workspace.
# Set a channel and text to post for real.
testData:
  config:
    defaultChannel: ""
  inputs:
    input: {}
  expect:
    output: "return output.output.ok === false && /required/.test(output.output.error)"
